newsitem.title: MEXICO: PAN senator attacks Mexican pension commissions.
newsitem.headline: PAN senator attacks Mexican pension commissions.

text.p: A combatative senator of the opposition National Action Party (PAN) on Thursday took aim at the private pension system, and suggested there would be changes if his party wins a Congressional majority in July.

In a statement, Jose Angel Conchello took issue with a rule forcing the central bank to charge commissions on those pension accounts that are not placed in the 17 private pension firms, known as Afores.
He said the rule bowed to the interests of foreign banks, who have major stakes in the 17 Afores.

He also accused Fernando Solis Soberon, head of the National Retirement Savings System Commission (Consar), of forcing Banco de Mexico to charge commissions held in the so-called Concentrator Account, which he said was beyond his brief.
Insured workers can either deposit their retirement savings in one of the Afores, or leave them for up to four years in the central bank's Concentrator Account.

Workers have protested the high levels of commissions charged by the Afores. But even those who shun them may be charged 1.44 percent of their base salary to leave them in the Concentrator Account, Conchello said in a statement.

"We hope that with the triumph of the opposition in the Congress (in mid-term elections on July 6), we can rescue the workers from the neoliberal slavery that the government plans, to serve international banks," he said.

The PAN, a conservative party that has a mixed attitude toward free market reform, is expected to pose a strong challenge to the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in the elections. The PRI has run Congress for 68 years.
